newsitem.title: USA: White House, states vow united front on tobacco.
newsitem.headline: White House, states vow united front on tobacco.

text.p: White House officials and the state attorneys general who brokered a settlement with the tobacco industry said on Thursday they were united in wanting to cut smoking, especially by children.
"We are united in a single cause to reduce smoking especially by children," White House domestic policy adviser Bruce Reed said after a meeting on the proposed settlement.

Reed and Health and Human Services Secretary Donna Shalala met at the White House with Mississippi Attorney General Mike Moore and Washington state Attorney General Christine Gregoire to review the $368.5 billion deal and discuss President Bill Clinton's concerns about it.

On Wednesday Clinton, in Madrid for a NATO summit, rejected as "unreasonable" a part of the proposed settlement that would restrict the government's hard-won powers to regulate the nicotine content of tobacco products.

Moore told reporters after Thursday's White House meeting that the deal was "very much alive" despite the president's objections and he would support any effort to strengthen it. But he said there were two sides to the settlement and the objective should be to get the deal put into law quickly to prevent more children from taking up the tobacco habit.

"If we can strengthen the language that we have proposed, that would be a good thing," Moore told reporters. "I think there is a little room, but not a whole lot of room, for tinkering with this agreement."
